title_en: The wrapped one and the cloaked one
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muzzammil, often rendered the wrapped one.
The one addressed is told to stand through the night except for a little: half of it, or a little less than that, or more than that; and to recite the Quran in measured fashion.
God says that He will cast upon the one addressed a weighty word.
The rising of the night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech.
By day the one addressed has long occupation.
The one addressed is told to remember the name of his Lord and to devote himself to Him with complete devotion.

chapters.summary_md: The passage calls on the one addressed as the wrapped one [c1]. He is told to stand through the night except for a little, and to recite the Quran in measured fashion [c2]. God says that He will cast upon him a weighty word [c3], and he is told to remember the name of his Lord and devote himself to Him [c6].
chapters.body_md:
The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muzzammil, often rendered the wrapped one [c1].

He is told to stand through the night except for a little: half of it, or a little less than that, or more than that; and to recite the Quran in measured fashion [c2]. God says that He will cast upon him a weighty word [c3].

The passage says that the rising of the night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech [c4], and that by day he has long occupation [c5]. He is told to remember the name of his Lord and to devote himself to Him with complete devotion [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The call and the commands are addressed to one person, whom the verses do not name [c1]. The commands are about the night [c2], and the passage gives reasons from the night and the day [c4][c5]. The weighty word that God will cast upon him is not described [c3]. The passage ends with remembrance and devotion [c6].
chapters.kids_md: The passage calls to someone who is wrapped up, and tells him to stand through the night except for a little [c1][c2]. He is told to recite the Quran slowly and clearly [c2]. He is told to remember the name of his Lord [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins the quiet of the night to speech that is more upright [c4]. Another is that it places remembrance of the Lord's name beside the long occupation of the day [c5][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who is addressed. The call is by a title and the verses name no one.
- Not established: why the one addressed is called the wrapped one, or what he was wrapped in; the verses give no circumstance.
- Not established: what the weighty word is, or when it was cast.
- Not established: for whom the standing through the night was meant beyond the one addressed, or for how long. The later verses of the same surah are outside this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the one addressed and the occasion of the call. Neither is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muddaththir, often rendered the cloaked one.
The one addressed is told to arise and warn.
He is told to magnify his Lord.
He is told to purify his garments; the Arabic word is read in more than one way.
He is told to keep away from ar-rujz, a word whose sense is disputed.
He is told not to give in order to gain more; the phrase is read in more than one way.
He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord.

chapters.summary_md: The passage calls on the one addressed as the cloaked one [c1]. He is told to arise and warn [c2], to magnify his Lord [c3], and to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].
chapters.body_md:
The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muddaththir, often rendered the cloaked one [c1].

He is told to arise and warn [c2], and to magnify his Lord [c3]. He is told to purify his garments; the Arabic word is read in more than one way [c4]. He is told to keep away from ar-rujz, a word whose sense is disputed [c5], and not to give in order to gain more, a phrase that is also read in more than one way [c6].

The passage ends by telling him to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].
chapters.deep_md: A series of short commands follow one another, and the passage gives no reason for any of them [c2][c3][c4][c5][c6][c7]. Some of them are read in more than one way: the word for garments, the word ar-rujz, and the phrase about giving in order to gain more [c4][c5][c6]. The warning has no stated object [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The passage calls to someone covered up, and tells him to arise and warn [c1][c2]. He is told to magnify his Lord [c3]. He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places patience for the sake of the Lord at the end of a series of commands [c7]. Another is that the commands to warn and to magnify the Lord stand side by side [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who is addressed, or why he is called the cloaked one. The call is by a title and the verses name no one.
- Not established: whom or what he was to warn; the verse has no object.
- Not established: what ar-rujz refers to, whether the garments in 74:4 are clothing or something else, or what the phrase about giving in order to gain more refers to.
- Not established: whether this passage came before or after the previous chapter's; the chapters follow the inventory order.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the one addressed and the occasion of the call. Neither is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of the calls, on who was addressed and on the order of the passages, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The titles al-muzzammil and al-muddaththir are in the Arabic as calls; their sense (wrapped, cloaked) is a rendering. The verses do not describe the condition of the one addressed.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the one addressed in both passages. The inventory title gives an identification that the verses themselves do not.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
